```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center", dpi = 300
)
library(vaxsurvR)
library(ggplot2)
PAL <- vcs_palette()
kbl <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "", ...)
pct <- function(x, d = 1) ifelse(is.na(x), "--", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), 100 * x))
```

Everything in this document is computed from `vcs_example`, the synthetic
survey shipped with the package: 600 households, 256 children, 14 antigens,
with a documented set of deliberately planted data-quality problems. No real
participant data appears anywhere. Every figure is produced by the function
named above it, so each page can be reproduced in one line.

# The shape of the workflow

```{r diagram, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.6, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "The five stages: plot\\_vcs\\_pipeline()"}
# Title and subtitle come from the section heading and the text below, so the
# figure carries neither. Label text is sized in millimetres while the boxes
# scale with the canvas, so base_size and fig.width move together: raising one
# without the other pushes the longer function names outside their box.
plot_vcs_pipeline(title = NULL, subtitle = NULL)
```

Read it top to bottom. The first row is the part people most often skip:
**the survey is described once**, in a schedule and a dictionary, and every
later call reads those two objects. That is what makes the same script run
against next round's export without editing a single function.

The two outlined boxes are optional. A survey whose questionnaire has no
caregiver-recall block simply omits them.

```{r pipeline-table}
p <- vcs_pipeline()
tab <- data.frame(
  Stage = p$stage,
  Step = p$fn,
  Required = ifelse(p$optional, "optional", "required"),
  `What it does` = p$caption,
  check.names = FALSE
)
kbl(tab, caption = "The pipeline as a table: vcs_pipeline()")
```

\newpage

# Configure: describe the survey once

The **schedule** says which antigens exist, the earliest age each dose may
validly be given, which dose precedes it and the minimum interval between
them. Nothing in the package assumes a country's calendar; these are the
numbers every later check reads.

```{r schedule}
s <- as.data.frame(vcs_example_schedule)
kbl(head(s[, c("vaccine", "antigen", "dose", "minimum_age_days",
                "maximum_age_days", "previous_dose", "minimum_interval_days")], 8),
    caption = "A vaccination schedule: vcs_schedule()",
    col.names = c("Vaccine", "Antigen", "Dose", "Min age (d)", "Max age (d)",
                  "After", "Min interval (d)"))
```

The **dictionary** maps the export's own variable names onto standardised
concepts. Wide exports encode repeat groups in the column name, so the
dictionary takes templates: `{c}` for the caregiver repeat, `{k}` for the
child, `{vv}` for the zero-padded vaccine index.

```{r dictionary}
d <- as.data.frame(vcs_example_dictionary)
kbl(head(d[, c("concept", "source", "level")], 10),
    caption = "Mapping source variables onto concepts: vcs_dictionary()",
    col.names = c("Concept", "Source variable", "Level"))
```

# Import: one object, three tables

`map_vcs_variables()` expands the repeat groups and returns a single object
holding the household, child and vaccination views side by side, with the raw
import carried along untouched.

```{r import}
counts <- summary(vcs_example)$counts
kbl(data.frame(Level = names(counts), N = as.integer(counts)),
    caption = "What the mapped object contains: map_vcs_variables()")
```

A child record is created wherever a repeat slot holds data, so empty slots in
a wide export never become phantom children.

\newpage

# Check: flag, never silently correct

`validate_vcs()` returns an object, not a printed warning. Every issue carries
a stable rule identifier, a severity and the record it concerns, so the result
can be filtered, joined, exported or handed to the field team.

```{r validate}
qa <- validate_vcs(vcs_example)
sev <- summary(qa, by = "severity")
kbl(as.data.frame(sev[, c("group", "n_issues", "n_records")]),
    caption = "Issues by severity: validate_vcs()",
    col.names = c("Severity", "Issues", "Records affected"))
```

```{r issue-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.6, out.width = "95%"}
by_rule <- summary(qa, by = "rule")
by_rule$group <- factor(by_rule$group, levels = rev(by_rule$group))
# Order the legend by severity rather than alphabetically.
by_rule$severity <- factor(by_rule$severity, levels = rev(vcs_severities()))
sev_cols <- c(INFO = PAL$secondary, WARNING = PAL$accent,
              ERROR = PAL$danger, CRITICAL = "#7B241C")
ggplot(by_rule, aes(x = .data$n_issues, y = .data$group, fill = .data$severity)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Issues", y = NULL,
       title = "Data-quality issues by rule",
       subtitle = "Flagged for investigation; no record is dropped") +
  theme_vcs(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
```

`clean_vcs()` then applies a ruleset. The default ruleset **flags and changes
nothing**; any rule that does change a value writes a log line naming the
record, the variable, the value before and after, the rule, its severity and
the time.

```{r clean}
cleaned <- clean_vcs(vcs_example)
kbl(as.data.frame(summary(cleaned$audit)),
    caption = "The audit trail: clean_vcs() then audit_changes()",
    col.names = c("Rule", "Action", "Severity", "Records", "Log entries"))
```

\newpage

# Derive: say what counts as vaccinated

A coverage figure is meaningless without the definition behind it. The package
grades the evidence for every dose and makes the definition an argument.

```{r evidence}
ev <- derive_evidence(vcs_example)$vaccinations$evidence
t <- as.data.frame(table(ev), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(t) <- c("Evidence", "Doses")
t$Share <- pct(t$Doses / sum(t$Doses))
kbl(t, caption = "Evidence grades: derive_evidence()")
```

`unknown` is not `none`. A dose with neither a card entry nor a recall answer
is unknown, and `derive_vaccination_status()` leaves it `NA` rather than
counting it as unvaccinated, unless you explicitly ask otherwise.

# Estimate: keep the design to the end

```{r estimate, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, out.width = "95%"}
VX <- c("BCG", "PENTA1", "PENTA3", "MCV1")
est <- estimate_coverage_by_evidence(vcs_example, vaccines = VX)
e <- as.data.frame(est)
e$indicator <- factor(e$indicator, levels = rev(VX))
ggplot(e, aes(x = .data$estimate, y = .data$indicator, colour = .data$evidence)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = .data$conf_low, xmax = .data$conf_high),
                 height = 0.22, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(v) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * v),
                     limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Card = PAL$info, Recall = PAL$accent,
                                 `Card or recall` = PAL$primary), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Coverage", y = NULL,
       title = "Coverage by source of evidence",
       subtitle = "estimate_coverage_by_evidence(); every child in every denominator") +
  theme_vcs(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
```

The card row is *documented* coverage, not coverage among card holders: a
child whose card was never seen counts as not documented, which is true. Pass
`denominator = "determinable"` for the other convention, and say in the report
which one a table uses.

```{r dropout}
d2 <- derive_vaccination_status(vcs_example)
des <- vcs_design(d2)
keep <- c("indicator", "method", "denominator", "estimate", "conf_low", "conf_high")
dr <- rbind(
  as.data.frame(estimate_dropout(des, "PENTA1", "PENTA3",
                                 method = "individual"))[, keep],
  as.data.frame(estimate_dropout(des, "PENTA1", "PENTA3",
                                 method = "coverage"))[, keep]
)
kbl(data.frame(
  Indicator = dr$indicator, Method = dr$method, n = dr$denominator,
  Estimate = pct(dr$estimate),
  `95% CI` = sprintf("%s -- %s", pct(dr$conf_low), pct(dr$conf_high)),
  check.names = FALSE
), caption = "Two definitions of dropout, both reported: estimate_dropout()")
```

\newpage

# Tracking fieldwork against the frame

Progress is measured against the **sampling frame**, not the data: a cluster
that was never visited leaves no trace in the export and can only come from
the frame.

```{r progress, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.6, out.width = "90%"}
raw <- vcs_example_frame_raw
frame <- read_psu_frame(primary = raw[raw$psu_type == "Primary", ],
                        backup  = raw[raw$psu_type == "Backup", ])
pm <- psu_map_data(vcs_example_raw, frame, psu_var = "psu_id",
                   zone_var = "health_zone", child_marker = "EC_ID",
                   n_caregivers = 2, n_children = 2)
plot_admin_progress_bars(admin_map_data(pm, "zone"), target = 0.8)
```

```{r funnel}
fn <- psu_map_summary(pm)
kbl(data.frame(
  Metric = c("Units in frame", "Units opened", "Units with children",
             "Units with no eligible child", "Children"),
  N = c(fn$primary_in_frame, fn$primary_opened, fn$primary_with_children,
        fn$primary_zero_children, fn$children)
), caption = "The sampling-unit funnel: psu_map_summary()")
```

Where a boundary layer is available, `plot_admin_map()` draws the same numbers
as a choropleth with the sampling units bubbled on top, and units holding no
data are drawn as "no data" rather than omitted.
